first_impression.reaction: My assistant opened it because a friend married on Paros and the family asked about it. The first screen is calm and sensible: areas, guest count, ceremony, where people sleep. Then the key takeaways say the biggest published figure is 150. Her summary was short: Paros is pretty, chapels everywhere, nothing published above 150, Petra Farm only takes 10 weddings a year, The Secret View lets you bring your own caterer, and Villa Mira can be taken whole but it's four villas. I read Petra Farm and The Secret View myself. The rest I skimmed.

journey.quote: The right one depends on your guest count, the ceremony you want (chapel, beach or terrace) and whether you would rather your guests sleep under the same roof.
journey.reaction: Guest count first and keeping guests under one roof. That's how I think about it too. No sunset talk.

journey.quote: Few Paros venues publish a wedding capacity, and the clearest figures belong to Petra Farm (a chapel for 120 and an event space for 150) and The Secret View (110 for a terrace ceremony, 120 for dinner).
journey.reaction: At least it's honest. But 150 is the top of it, and we are 200 to 400. My assistant would put Paros in the 'pre-wedding dinner, not the wedding' pile right here unless someone tells me otherwise.

journey.section: Hotel, estate, villa or event venue
journey.quote: If a venue offers its own wedding package, our guide to [Greece wedding packages](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages) sets out how to weigh it against booking the venue on its own terms.
journey.reaction: Packages again, right when I'm deciding what kind of place I want. I'm not buying a package.

journey.quote: For the rest, ask whether the wedding spaces, or the whole property, can be closed to other guests.
journey.reaction: The right question, put the right way. Someone understands that a private terrace and a closed hotel are not the same thing.

journey.quote: **Rooms:** 46 suites for 2 to 4 people (4 executive and 42 junior) and 11 double rooms, with marble bathrooms from Naxos and verandas or balconies.
journey.reaction: A real room count, which I appreciate. It's also too small to hold the family, never mind the guests. If we could close it, it might work for the close family only.

journey.quote: For a smaller wedding that wants its own chapel and a pool, Anemoi keeps everything to a few steps.
Arriving by boat at the dock is the detail guests will remember.
journey.reaction: Arriving by sea is how I'd want guests to come in, away from the road. But it's a beach bar in a park, so I'd want to know who else is on that beach.

journey.quote: **Standout:** The farm limits itself to 10 weddings a year, and its team is on site to oversee every supplier for the whole rental period.
journey.reaction: Ten a year. That's the kind of scarcity that tells me they protect each wedding. And their own team watching every supplier matters for discretion.

journey.section: Pyrgaki Hotel, above the gulf of Parikia
journey.quote: **Standout:** The hotel lists fireworks, a live orchestra, a DJ, a horse-drawn carriage for the bride and a white car for the groom among the services it can arrange.
journey.reaction: A carriage for the bride and a white car for the groom reads like an add-on menu from a brochure. That's not how our wedding gets planned.

journey.section: Villa Mira Paros, above the Bay of Parikia
journey.quote: **Exclusive use:** Yes; the whole property can be booked, with a shared barbecue and pool area.
journey.reaction: Whole-property booking is what I'd ask for. 'Shared barbecue' and a kitchen in every villa make it sound like a family holiday rental, though.

journey.quote: **Standout:** Two children's pools and a family-friendly approach make it a natural base for guests travelling with young children.
journey.reaction: Useful. There will be many small children in our family, and they stay with us.

journey.section: The Secret View at Fladakia Estate, above Golden Beach
journey.quote: **Exclusive use:** Couples have full access to every area of the venue for 24 hours.
journey.reaction: Good, it's in print. But our celebrations run over three days, not one, so 24 hours is only the start of the conversation.

journey.section: The Secret View at Fladakia Estate, above Golden Beach
journey.quote: You may bring your own suppliers, and the venue suggests a site inspection for your caterer.
journey.reaction: This matters most to my mother. If we can bring our own caterer, the food can be done properly for the family.

journey.quote: Expect crowds and heat at the busy ports from May to October, and stairs to carry luggage up and down.
journey.reaction: Carrying luggage up stairs. My guests won't be on a ferry. Nothing here about private aircraft into Paros, private boats or cars meeting people.

journey.quote: Public KTEL buses link the villages with each other and with Parikia and Naoussa all year, and summer routes, especially to Naoussa, run into the early morning.
journey.reaction: Bus timetables. My assistant would delete this paragraph from her summary. It tells me who the page was written for, and it isn't me.

journey.quote: For a summer date, plan shade, a later ceremony and a covered fallback.
journey.reaction: Calm and practical about heat and wildfire. My security people would want this thought through.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, [Smartraveller](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/planning-trip/advice-your-planned-activities/getting-married-overseas) says some countries ask you to prove you are free to marry, most often with a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and registry certificates.
journey.reaction: Our lawyers handle this, and we are not only Australian. Skipped.

journey.section: Shortlist your Paros venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The next step is finding out which of them are free on your date, on your terms.
journey.reaction: 'On your terms' is the right note. Quiet, not eager.

journey.section: Shortlist your Paros venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One person throughout, yes. 'For Australian couples' makes me wonder whether a family split between Dubai, Sydney and London is who they had in mind.

unanswered_questions: Can any Paros venue, or a combination of venues, hold 200 to 400 guests for a seated dinner?
Can Petra Farm, Astir of Paros or Poseidon be closed to the public for three days for different family events?
Can private aircraft land at Paros Airport, and can private boats and cars be arranged for every guest?
Can our own security team work alongside each venue's, and how are staff phones, suppliers and guest photography controlled?
Beyond The Secret View, which venues let us bring our own caterer for family dietary needs?
Have they delivered a wedding of our scale in the Cyclades, and is there a private or referral channel to someone senior?

turn_offs_found.quote: If a venue offers its own wedding package, our guide to [Greece wedding packages](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages) sets out how to weigh it against booking the venue on its own terms.
turn_offs_found.why: It turns up exactly where I'm deciding what kind of place I want, and it treats a package as the normal thing to compare against. That's how a standard client is handled, and being handled like one is what I'm afraid of.

turn_offs_found.quote: **Standout:** The hotel lists fireworks, a live orchestra, a DJ, a horse-drawn carriage for the bride and a white car for the groom among the services it can arrange.
turn_offs_found.why: Listing a carriage and a white car as the standout reads like a menu of extras you tick off. It makes the venue, and the page, feel pitched at a set-piece hotel wedding, not a bespoke one.

turn_offs_found.quote: Public KTEL buses link the villages with each other and with Parikia and Naoussa all year, and summer routes, especially to Naoussa, run into the early morning.
turn_offs_found.why: Bus routes, ferry crowds and carrying luggage up port stairs explain things I will never do, and say nothing about private arrival. Arrival logistics are exactly what I judge a planner on, so this section makes the brand look ordinary.

would_share_with: My assistant, to ask Petra Farm and The Secret View whether they can stretch beyond their published figures or run across several days
My mother, for the line about bringing our own caterer at The Secret View
Nobody else; on this page, Paros looks like a place for a pre-wedding dinner, not the wedding itself

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Paros venues with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=paros-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The close is quiet and I like that. But nothing on Paros fits our numbers, nothing shows they've handled our scale, and I don't fill in web forms. If a friend referred them for Greece as a whole, my assistant might call.

top_3_changes: Rework 'Getting to Paros' so it doesn't lead with public transport (KTEL buses, ferry crowds, carrying luggage up port stairs). Cover private arrival (private aircraft at PAS, private boats, cars meeting guests) only where it can be confirmed; Monastiri's sea arrival at its dock is already on the page and could be mentioned here.

In 'Capacity, rooms and exclusive use', add one plain sentence that the largest published figure on this list is 150 (Petra Farm's event space), so a family planning a larger wedding knows at once to ask about combining spaces or to look at the wider Greece guide. That saves my assistant reading eight entries to find out.

Remove the 'Greece wedding packages' link from 'Hotel, estate, villa or event venue', and trim the Pyrgaki standout to the fireworks and live orchestra rather than the carriage and white car. Both make the page read like a list of add-ons.
